subject: Issue with "QCA" Package Version 19 - Bug in the "truthTable" Function

messages.author: ffcfcd28353e49b7
messages.subject: Issue with "QCA" Package Version 19 - Bug in the "truthTable" Function
parts:
Dear Adrian Dusa,

I am writing to bring to your attention a bug in the latest version of the "QCA" package (version 19) for the R programming language.

During my recent usage of the package, I discovered an issue specifically related to the "truthTable" function when it is used with 8 or more conditions as arguments. It appears that in these cases, the function fails to execute correctly and returns an error. However, when the number of conditions is fewer than 8, the "truthTable" function works flawlessly without any errors (Tested on Mac and Windows systems).

To confirm this behavior, I compared it with the previous version of the package (version 18), and I can confirm that the "truthTable" function worked perfectly fine with 8 or more conditions in that version.

I wanted to bring this bug to your attention so that you are aware of the issue and can take the necessary steps to address it. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter, and I appreciate your efforts in maintaining the "QCA" package.

This is my data set: forFuzzy.csv

And the following code returns an error:

write_csv(x = forFuzzy, file = "forFuzzy.csv")

TT <- truthTable(data = as.data.frame(forFuzzy),
                 outcome = "OUTC",
                 conditions = c("C1", "C2", "C3", "C4", "C5", "C6", "C7", "C8") ,
                 incl.cut =  0.94,
                 sort.by = "incl, n",
                 show.cases = TRUE,
                 n.cut=10)
TT

Note that by removing any of the conditions, the code works perfectly. Is there a limit of 7 conditions in this new version?

Thanks for your attention,

Pedro Carmona

messages.author: 53dbab5845ace6b6
messages.subject: Re: Issue with "QCA" Package Version 19 - Bug in the "truthTable" Function
parts:
Dear Pedro,

You are quite right, this was an unintentional side-effect of solving (as per the ChangeLog file) a different bug affecting the printing of row names n.cut is greater than 1.
It seems that solving that led to this, which I have (now) also solved in my development version.

Will release a patch version soon, thanks very much for this report,
Adrian

messages.subject: Re: Issue with "QCA" Package Version 19 - Bug in the "truthTable" Function
parts:
Assuming you are on Windows, the link below points to a .zip file that is a binary build of the newest development version:
https://artifacts.r-hub.io/QCA_3.19.1.tar.gz-fbf4d00441a42410f48f5feca3853b0e/QCA_3.19.1.zip

It can be installed from R, using the menu:

Packages / Install package(s) from local files...

or from RStudio, click on Install in the Packages tab, and use Install from: Package Archive File (.zip; .tar.gz)

If using Linux or MacOS, I can send either the source (.tar.gz) file which needs the necessary build tools installed, or for MacOS I can send my own binary package.

Hope this helps,
Adrian
